panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: How long the Argo CD API server has been running. A value that keeps resetting is a crash loop: read the server's pod events.

panels.title: Clusters
panels.description: Destination clusters Argo CD manages. A number that changes with no planned cluster change means a cluster was removed or its credentials expired.

panels.title: Applications
panels.description: Applications matching the health, sync and destination filters above. Compare with the total to see how much is in trouble.

panels.title: Repositories
panels.description: Distinct Git repositories the applications track. Use it as a scale figure; an unexpected drop is applications that lost their source.

panels.title: Operations
panels.description: Applications with a sync or refresh operation in flight now. A number that stays high for long is a stuck operation: open the application and read its operation state.

panels.title: Applications over time
panels.description: Applications by the chosen grouping over time. A step is applications added or removed; a slow slide is applications leaving the selected filters.

panels.title: Health Status
panels.description: Applications by health status over time. Anything other than Healthy for long, especially Degraded or Missing, needs a look: open the application and read the failing resource.

panels.title: Sync Status
panels.description: Applications by sync status over time. OutOfSync that persists means Git and the cluster disagree and nothing is reconciling it: check auto-sync and the last sync result.

panels.title: Sync Activity
panels.description: Syncs started in each interval, by the chosen grouping. A burst is a deploy or a sync loop; a flat zero on a busy estate is a controller that stopped.

panels.title: Sync Failures
panels.description: Syncs that ended in Error or Failed in each interval. Should be zero. Open the affected application and read the sync result message.

panels.title: Reconciliation Activity
panels.description: Application reconciliations in each interval, by the chosen grouping. A sudden rise is a resync storm; a fall to zero means the application controller is not reconciling.

panels.title: Reconciliation Performance
panels.description: Distribution of how long an application reconcile takes. A band that moves up means slow Git or a heavy manifest: compare with the repo server panels.

panels.title: K8s API Activity
panels.description: Kubernetes API requests the controller made in each interval, by verb and resource kind. A spike is a resync or a cluster watch restarting; sustained high volume can throttle the API server.

panels.title: Workqueue Depth
panels.description: Items waiting in the application controller's work queues. A depth that does not drain means reconciles are slower than changes arrive: check the controller's CPU and the repo server.

panels.title: Pending kubectl run
panels.description: kubectl commands the controller has queued and not started. A number that grows means the controller is short of exec capacity.

panels.title: Controller memory usage
panels.description: Go heap allocated by the application controller. A steady climb over days is a leak or a growing estate; a jump on restart is the cluster cache filling.

panels.title: Controller CPU usage
panels.description: CPU seconds per second used by the application controller. Sustained near its limit means reconciles queue behind it.

panels.title: Controller goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines in the application controller. A count that only grows is a leak; compare with memory.

panels.title: Resource Objects Count
panels.description: Kubernetes objects Argo CD caches per destination cluster. Growth is the estate growing; it also sizes the controller's memory.

panels.title: API Resources Count
panels.description: API resource kinds Argo CD watches per destination cluster. A change with no CRD change points at a cluster upgrade or a broken discovery.

panels.title: Cluster Events Count
panels.description: Cluster events the controller processed in each interval, per destination cluster. Sustained high volume is a noisy workload driving reconciles.

panels.title: Git Requests (ls-remote)
panels.description: Git ls-remote calls the repo server made in each window, to detect new commits. A rise means more applications or a shorter refresh interval; failures show in sync errors.

panels.title: Git Requests (checkout)
panels.description: Git fetches the repo server made in each window, to render manifests. A rise is new commits or cache misses; sustained high volume loads the Git host.

panels.title: Git Fetch Performance
panels.description: Distribution of Git fetch durations. A band that moves up is a slow Git host or network: sync latency follows.

panels.title: Git Ls-Remote Performance
panels.description: Distribution of Git ls-remote durations. A band that moves up delays the detection of new commits.

panels.title: API server memory used
panels.description: Go heap allocated by the Argo CD API server. A steady climb is a leak; a jump follows a restart.

panels.title: API server goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines in the Argo CD API server. A count that only grows is a leak; compare with memory.

panels.title: Repo server memory used
panels.description: Go heap allocated by the repo server. Large manifests and many parallel renders raise it; a steady climb is a leak.

panels.title: Repo server goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines in the repo server. A count that only grows is a leak; compare with memory.

panels.title: GC Time Quantiles
panels.description: Go garbage-collection pause of the API server, worst case. Long pauses mean memory pressure: compare with the memory panel.

panels.title: ApplicationService Requests
panels.description: gRPC calls to the API server's Application service in each interval, by method and result code. Non-OK codes are the ones to read: a rise in errors on a method is a failing feature or a client misbehaving.

panels.title: ClusterService Requests
panels.description: gRPC calls to the API server's Cluster service in each interval, by method and result code. Non-OK codes are the ones to read: a rise in errors on a method is a failing feature or a client misbehaving.

panels.title: ProjectService Requests
panels.description: gRPC calls to the API server's Project service in each interval, by method and result code. Non-OK codes are the ones to read: a rise in errors on a method is a failing feature or a client misbehaving.

panels.description: gRPC calls to the API server's Session service in each interval, by method and result code. Non-OK codes are the ones to read: a rise in errors on a method is a failing feature or a client misbehaving.

panels.title: AccountService Requests
panels.description: gRPC calls to the API server's Account service in each interval, by method and result code. Non-OK codes are the ones to read: a rise in errors on a method is a failing feature or a client misbehaving.

panels.title: SettingsService Requests
panels.description: gRPC calls to the API server's Settings service in each interval, by method and result code. Non-OK codes are the ones to read: a rise in errors on a method is a failing feature or a client misbehaving.

panels.title: Requests by result
panels.description: Redis requests made by Argo CD components, split by whether they failed. The failed series should be zero; a rise means Redis is unavailable or slow and the UI and controller cache suffer.
